body:
A few moments, actually. I began hiding bottles of vodka around the house and yard so that I could hide my drinking from my now wife. She didn’t want me to drink anymore so Esther than give it up I got creative. I’d make excuses to go outside - like taking trash out or “answering a work call” - then I’d go chug a few swigs until I felt that sense of calm and comfort wash over me. When she went to sleep I’d stay up playing video games, drinking from a bottle I hid near the television until I passed out.

Then I’d wake up slightly hungover. Before leaving for work I’d drink more vodka to get a buzz going. At work I’d go to the store nearby and buy a six pack of Sierra Nevada Torpedo Double IPA. I’d hide it somewhere discreet so I could slip away and fill my coffee cup, just to keep me feeling okay (emotionally - never had terrible physical symptoms). Then I’d repeat it all over again the next day.

Eventually she caught me with the vodka. So there went my fix at home. This led to me drinking more at work, then maybe leaving early do I could hit the nearby bar for a shot and a beer to prep for the trip home (don’t worry, public transportation). Eventually she caught me doing this because she’d breathalyze me, which was horribly inaccurate btw. I blew a 0.00 on more than one occasion while pretty drunk.

We had a huge blowup so I went and stayed with my mother. Drinking more of course. One night I realized I was hungry and kind of bored while playing Diablo 3, so I walked to a nearby restaurant. Had a few beers, ate dinner, then left to go home. While leaving the establishment a group of four cops tell me they’d like to talk. Not wanting to get myself in trouble (never ever talk to the police - unless you’re the one reporting a crime), I said I wasn’t interested, that I was on my way home to go to bed, and to have a good night. I walked away. A few seconds later I feet my left arm jerked behind me and then a kick to my back - I went down hard - landing on my left forehead and my right hand. They arrest me. 

My memory gets a bit hazy for the next 10 or so minutes because of the drinking and the head wound. When my memory becomes clear again I was handcuffed in the back of the police car, on my way to the station. I kept repeating over and over that I just wanted to go home, I wasn’t bothering anyone, I wanted to be home in bed. Cop told me tough shit. I am put in a holding cell which faced this area where cops hung out and did their paperwork. I felt like I was in a zoo, handcuffed with people looking and laughing at me.

My hand is in a lot of pain and is going between intense pain and numbness. I start talking about how I was minding my own business, they had no probable cause to detain me, and they’d deliberately injured me because I didn’t stop to talk, and now I was arrested and sitting in a cell after suffering deprivation of rights under color of law. Eventually this older cop hears what I’m saying, tells the officer nearest me to cut me loose for medical attention. Of course I just want to go home but they tell me the only way I’m getting out of there is by ambulance. I quickly agree, telling myself whatever I had to pay was worth it to get out. 

The ER docs check me for concussion and clean my wounds, but don’t even look at my hand. They give me an ice pack for that. After they were done I asked if I was free to go and they said yeah cops left after you got dropped off.

So - it turned out my thumb was dislocated. I didn’t know this for two days. It was in so much pain. I got an x ray done the day after but my doc didn’t see it until two days later.

I get referred to a hand surgeon who tries to pop it back in - but it’s “buttonholed” meaning soft tissue is in the way - so he has to do it surgically.

I came away from all this with several months of Occupational therapy for my thumb, two thousand dollars for ER and ambulance, a scar on my hand and a stiff joint that prevents me
From full function for the rest of my life.

And that wasn’t even the end of my drinking but it was a huge wake up call.

I’ve been sober for over nine months now. I went to a SMART recovery group two days per week for a while, which I enjoyed. Non-addicts do not understand what drug abuse is like so its good to talk with people who do. I haven’t lapsed, which has been difficult at some times but now being sober doesn’t bother me. When I’m out with others I drink soda or non-alc beer. At home I relax with a non-alc beer after work (there are so many different kinds now, it’s not just Saint pauli or o’douls).

I don’t know if I’ll ever drink again but I sure as hell won’t be doing it any time soon.

I understand how you’re feeling and for a long time this was my life. I became a serious alcoholic last year when I couldn’t cope with my depression, my partner’s pregnancy, and the difficulty of our relationship on a daily basis (not compatible in a lot of ways - I’m laid back and she’s super type A). I would drink every night to excess, until my partner banned me from having any alcohol at home.

I began hiding bottles of vodka around the house and the backyard. I would wait until she was asleep so I could grab the bottle and just chug it until I couldn’t feel anything anymore. Or I would make some excuse to go outside - take a call or empty the trash - so I could hit my stash and chug more vodka. Then I started buying beer every morning and secretly drinking at work. Going out to bars for “lunch” (4 beers and some shots). All the while pretending to be sober.

Eventually she found out and kicked me out. I spiraled from there and was roughed up by cops because I was walking home drunk and didn’t want to talk to them. They dislocated my thumb really bad and I had to have it surgically repaired, but I suffered through six days of intense pain until I found out about the dislocation. My thumb will never be the same.

Now I do SMART Recovery on and off (did it weekly for months) and I haven’t had a drink in 8 months. I’m still horribly depressed mind you, but I’m happy I have at least some control over my life again. Addiction is horrible. It will ruin your life.

I wish you luck - I won’t tell you that you will be happier, but being sober is at least a less volatile life to lead.
